What this project is

Notes · start here

The goal is to generate interfaces that are customizable, by generating them from a design space of UI patterns instead of straight from a prompt.

The goal

Generated interfaces should be customizable by default. The customization features come with the interface — they are not bolted on afterwards.

Right now a generated screen is frozen. You get what the model picked, and if you want it different you ask for a new one.

How

Don’t generate the interface directly. Generate a UI specification first, and build that spec out of a design space of patterns. This atlas is that design space.

  • A pattern is a known way to do a UI job — overview–detail, search, dashboard.
  • Each pattern has a design space: the dimensions you can vary.
  • Each dimension has variations. One variation per dimension is one interface.
  • Those picks are the spec, and the spec is what gets generated from.
  • Any dimension you leave open becomes a customization feature the user gets.

Why do it this way

Generating from a design space means the alternatives are already named. The interface knows what it could have been, so it can offer that choice to whoever is using it.

Generating from a prompt alone throws those alternatives away. Nothing is left to hand the user a control over.

The papers call this malleability. Same thing — how much of the interface the end user can change.

What’s in here

  • — every pattern with its dimensions and variations. 119 entries.
  • — the 12 kinds of dimension every pattern is tagged with.
  • — the 11 stages for building a design space like this.
  • — the spec format a generated interface is written in.
  • — where the gap is biggest: patterns that could be customizable but aren’t in real apps.
  • — how existing pattern catalogs map onto the atlas.

Where to start

Open the Atlas and click any card. The Configure block on a card is the whole idea in miniature: pick variations, and the spec below updates.

archetype · browse-collections

Browse collections

Scan many comparable things, narrow to the relevant few, and focus on one — the activity behind shopping, inboxes, file systems and search results alike.

Anatomy

  • Collection — The whole set, in some organizing structure
  • Item representation — How one item stands for itself inside the collection
  • Focus — The deeper look at one item, wherever it opens

Design space

Item representation content

How much of each item does the collection show, and in what abstracted form?

depth Depth per item one
aggregate Collection-level abstraction many

Organization composition

What structure holds the items, and how many collections are in play?

structure Structure one
multiplicity Multiplicity one

Arrangement layout

How are items placed on the screen?

arrangement Arrangement one

Narrowing and scale scope

How does a person get from everything to the few that matter, and how much is present at once?

narrowing Narrowing mechanisms many
portion Portion present one

Configure


    
In the wild
Productivity tools let people switch arrangement and grouping routinely; consumer products rarely do. CHI '25 measured 8.33% for overview–detail on the web.
  • Notion databases — Table, board, list, gallery, calendar and timeline views of one database
  • Craigslist — Several listing layouts from a menu
  • Finder — Icon, list, column and gallery views per folder

    
Techniques · signature Arrangement morphing
  • Arrangement morphing (Arrangement) — Switch arrangement while keeping the selection, the surfaced attributes and the scroll anchor, so a list becomes a board or a map without losing your place.
  • Surface, then organize (Narrowing and scale) — Any attribute surfaced into the item representation becomes a sort key, a filter and a grouping, generalizing CHI '25’s surface-then-sort finding to every collection.
  • Describe the grouping · AI (Organization) — Ask for a structure in words (“group by what I’d need for the trip”); the model proposes a generated attribute and the grouping that uses it, both inspectable.

    
Protocol
Sample. App Store and Google Play top charts in every category, plus Similarweb top sites; code every screen whose main job is showing many comparable items.
Unit. One presentation of one collection (a screen can hold several).

      
Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.72 first pass → 0.93 final; all three agree on 82% → 96% of cells. 4 variations adopted of 6 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 5 unobserved variations.

    

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Hoarders keep every attribute visible while minimalists strip the representation down (observed for overview–detail; expected to hold for any collection)
  • People reshape a collection mid-task, not only at the start

    
Questions
  • Is there one collection grammar under list, board, map and timeline, or do some arrangements need their own?
  • How should a collection carry its customization across products?

Comparison table

        
A few selected items side by side against shared attributes, so that differences can be read and a choice made.

      

    

    
Anatomy
  • Item columns — The items being compared
  • Attribute rows — The criteria
  • Difference cues — What stands out
  • Add and remove — Changing the set

    
Design space
Criteria content
Which attributes become rows, and how are values shown?
criteria Attribute selection one
valueForm Value form many
Item set composition
Where do the compared items come from?
origin Origin of items one

      
      
    
Orientation layout
Which way do items and criteria run?
orientation Orientation one
sticky Sticky parts many
Difference emphasis feedback
How are differences made to stand out?
emphasis Emphasis one
Decision support scope
Does the table help conclude, not only compare?
decision Decision support many

    
Configure

    
In the wild
Choosing the items is common; choosing the criteria, or weighting them, is rare outside research systems.
  • Amazon — Compare with similar items
  • Mesh (UIST '20) — Users build comparison criteria while researching

    
Techniques · signature Criteria weaving
  • Criteria weaving (Criteria) — Drag an attribute from any item’s detail into the table to add a row; weight rows by dragging them up; collapse identical rows.
  • Fill the gaps · AI (Criteria) — When an item lacks a row’s value, a model searches its data and fills it with provenance, or answers Not Specified (CHI '25 consistent values).
  • Ask which is better for… · AI (Decision support) — “Which is better for a small apartment?” adds the criteria the answer depends on, weighted and editable, instead of a bare verdict.

    
Protocol
Sample. Retail compare features, SaaS pricing pages, insurance and finance comparison sites, plus research systems for decision-making.
Unit. One comparison of two or more items.

      
Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.59 first pass → 0.93 final; all three agree on 75% → 95% of cells. 2 variations adopted of 3 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 3 unobserved variations.

    

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Criteria emerge during comparison, not before it (Mesh)

    
Questions
  • When should a comparison table conclude, and when should it stay neutral?

Items as rows against attributes as columns, built for scanning, comparing, sorting, filtering and acting on many items at once.

  • Row — One item
  • Cell — One attribute value
  • Toolbar — Collection operations
  • Footer — Aggregates and paging

    
Design space
Columns and cells content
Which attributes become columns, and how are values rendered?

cellRendering Cell rendering many
Density and structure layout
How tightly are rows packed, what stays put, and how do rows expand?

frozen Frozen regions many
rowExpansion Row expansion one
Selection and operations scope

opScope Operations apply to many

Configure

    
In the wild
In productivity and admin software, showing, hiding, reordering and resizing columns, sorting, filtering and grouping are routine.
  • Airtable — Hide fields, group, sort, filter and row height per view
  • Excel / Google Sheets — Freeze, filter, sort and pivot
  • Jira list view — Choose columns

    
Techniques · signature Column surfacing
  • Column surfacing (Columns and cells) — Pull any attribute from a record’s detail straight into a column, the tabular form of Fluid Attributes; hide columns back into the detail.
  • Formula by example · AI (Columns and cells) — Type the value you want in two or three cells and the table proposes the computed column.
  • Table ↔ cards morph (Narrow screens) — The same column set reflows to cards when narrow, with pinned columns becoming the card’s title and subtitle roles.
  • Ask for a column · AI (Columns and cells) — “Add a column for whether the paper has a user study” extracts a value per row, with provenance and an Unknown value.

    
Protocol
Sample. Admin consoles, CRMs, analytics tools, banking and brokerage sites, plus grid libraries’ showcase apps.
Unit. One table over one record set.

      
Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.64 first pass → 0.89 final; all three agree on 76% → 93% of cells. 1 variation adopted of 1 proposed; 1 unresolved cell; 1 unobserved variation.

    

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Power users build wide tables and scroll; occasional users want a few columns and a detail panel

    
Questions
  • When does a data table become a spreadsheet, and should people be able to cross that line?

Feed

        
An unbounded, continuously arriving stream of heterogeneous items, ordered by time or by ranking and consumed by scrolling.

      

    

    
Anatomy
  • Stream — The scrolling container and its loading edge
  • Post — One item: author, body, media, engagement
  • Injected modules — Non-post units placed into the stream
  • Ranking — The invisible policy that decides order

    
Design space
Post content content
How much of each post appears, and how uniform are the items?
density Density one
heterogeneity Heterogeneity many
Ordering and sources initiative
Who decides what appears, and in what order?
ordering Ordering one

      
    
sources Sources many

      
      
    
Arrangement layout
How is the stream laid out?
arrangement Arrangement one
Loading and position lifecycle
How does new content arrive, and does the feed remember where you were?
loading Loading many

      
    
position End and position one
Nesting composition
Do posts contain other posts?
nesting Nesting many

      
      
    

    
Configure

    
In the wild
Source and ordering choices are increasingly exposed; representation and density almost never are.
  • Bluesky — Pin and switch between custom feeds
  • Reddit — Sort by Best, Hot, New, Top, Rising
  • TweetDeck / X Pro — Compose columns from searches and lists
  • Instagram — Following and Favorites feed options

    
Techniques · signature Feed recipes
  • Feed recipes (Ordering and sources) — The ranking policy becomes an editable recipe — sources × filters × weights — that can be read, tuned, saved as a column and shared, just as Meridian made an ODI exchangeable.
  • Density dial (Post content) — Semantic zoom over posts: pinch from headline to card to full post, choosing which attributes survive each level.
  • Mute by attribute (Post content) — Surface hidden attributes (is a repost, has a link, is sponsored) and filter by them, making every attribute a lever.
  • Because-you-said · AI (Ordering and sources) — “Show me less of this, because it’s rage bait” becomes an explicit, inspectable constraint in the recipe rather than an opaque signal.

    
Protocol
Sample. Top 20 apps in Social Networking, News and Entertainment charts on both app stores, plus their web versions.
Unit. One feed surface (home, following, a topic feed) within one app.

      
Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.73 first pass → 0.93 final; all three agree on 84% → 96% of cells. 6 variations adopted of 7 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 2 unobserved variations.

    

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Grazers scroll ambiently while completionists want an end state
  • Recipes tuned once, then ignored unless the feed drifts

    
Questions
  • How much ranking transparency helps before it overwhelms?
  • Can a feed recipe transfer across platforms the way a Meridian spec transfers across shops?

In the wild
Desktop file managers have long let people choose views, columns, icon sizes, sorting and grouping per folder.
  • Finder — View options per folder, including columns shown and groups
  • Windows Explorer — Layout, details columns and grouping
  • macOS — Smart Folders as saved queries

    
Techniques · signature Per-folder lenses
  • Per-folder lenses (Item view) — A folder carries its own view spec that can be copied to other folders or promoted to a default.
  • Surface from Get Info (Metadata) — Surface any property from a file’s info panel as a column or thumbnail badge across the folder.
  • Organize by description · AI (Grouping) — “Group these by project” proposes generated tags you can accept per file.

    
Protocol
Sample. Operating-system file managers, cloud drives, and file pickers inside creative and office suites.
Unit. One location view within one file manager.

      
Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.80 first pass → 0.94 final; all three agree on 85% → 96% of cells. 1 variation adopted of 2 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 3 unobserved variations.

    

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Pilers keep flat folders and search; filers build deep trees

    
Questions
  • Should views follow the folder, the task, or the file type?

Anatomy

  • Column — A value of the grouping attribute
  • Card — One item’s key attributes
  • Swimlane — An optional second grouping across columns

    
Design space
Grouping composition
What do columns and swimlanes stand for?
columns Column source one
swimlanes Swimlanes one

      
    
Card and column content content
What does each card and column say about its items?
cardFields Card attributes many

      
    
columnSummary Column summaries many
Transitions flow

Configure

    
In the wild
Productivity boards expose grouping, card fields and filters, often as an admin setting rather than a personal one.
  • Jira — Configure columns, swimlanes and card layout fields
  • Linear — Display options for grouping, ordering and visible properties
  • Notion — Group by any property, choose card preview and properties

    
Techniques · signature Fluid Grouping
  • Fluid Grouping (Grouping) — Drag any attribute from a card’s detail onto the column header strip and the board regroups by it; drag a second one onto the lane gutter for swimlanes. Fluid Attributes, applied to structure.
  • Transition preview (Transitions) — While dragging, the target column says what the drop will change: the new value, required fields and the automations it will fire.
  • Surface card fields (Card and column content) — Surface or hide attributes from the card detail into every card, per board and per person.
  • Generated columns · AI (Grouping) — “Group these by risk” creates an AI-generated attribute with sources and uses it as the column source; wrong values can be dragged to correct them.

    
Protocol
Sample. Project-management, CRM, applicant-tracking and help-desk products (G2 category leaders), plus GitHub and GitLab.
Unit. One board configuration over one set of items.

      
Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.62 first pass → 0.91 final; all three agree on 73% → 94% of cells. 3 variations adopted of 4 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 5 unobserved variations.

      
Unreliable sub-dimensions. cardSize

    

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Teams keep one canonical board while individuals want personal card fields
  • Regrouping is used as a thinking move (by risk, by owner), not only for workflow

    
Questions
  • Should a personal grouping change the shared board for others?
  • How are illegal transitions shown before the drop?

Overview–detail

        
An overview of many items, each shown through a few key attributes, paired with a detail view that shows many or all attributes of a selected item.

      

    

    
Anatomy
  • Overview — Organizes the collection with a structure (list, grid, map…) and its affordances
  • Item view — Represents one item inside the overview through key attributes
  • Detail view — Shows all attributes of one item, opened from the overview

    
Design space
Content content
Is information shown in the overview, the detail view or both, and how are overview attributes abstracted from detail attributes?
attributePlacement Attribute is shown… many
abstraction Overview abstractions many
truncation Long text in the overview one
Composition composition
How are multiple overviews and detail views connected?
relationship Relationships one
recursion Recursion many
linking Linking across overviews one
Layout layout
How are overviews and detail views arranged, how are items organized, and how many details are open?
openIn Overview–detail arrangement one
overviewType Overview layout many
detailMultiplicity Detail views open one
Invocation invocation
What opens a detail view, from which part of the item, and how does a person get back?
openBy Opened by many
openFrom Opened from one
Scope of attributes scope
Do attributes describe one item, or the whole collection?
attributeScope Attribute scope many

    
Configure

    
In the wild
Measured, not estimated: 13 of 156 websites (8.33%) offered any customization; content 2.56%, composition 0%, layout 7.69%. At most eight layout variations on one site (CHI '25 §3.3).
  • Craigslist — Five overview layouts and three overview–detail layouts; grid shows thumbnails, list does not
  • eBay — Toggle six attributes in results
  • Gmail — Reading pane on the right, below, or off

    
Techniques · signature Fluid Attributes
  • Fluid Attributes (Content) — In Attributes Mode, select attributes in the detail view and Surface them into every item of the overview, or Hide them; drag attributes between views directly (CHI '25 §4.1.1).
  • Sort and filter by any attribute (Content) — Any surfaced attribute becomes sortable and filterable, including interactive ones: sort by the wishlist boolean to pin items (CHI '25 §4.1.2).
  • AI-assisted Fluid Attributes · AI (Content) — Ask “how popular are these items?” to surface Watchers and Items Sold; generate new attributes such as Total Cost with inspectable sources; reformat inconsistent titles; fill missing values or answer Not Specified (CHI '25 §4.1.3).
  • Tabbed multiple overviews (Composition) — Add, rename and remove overviews as tabs, used to split a task into sub-collections (CHI '25 §4.2).
  • Layout menus and attribute-invoked overviews (Layout) — Dropdowns for overview and overview–detail layout; selecting Price and Feedback Score offers a scatter plot, and a generated colour attribute offers a colour space (CHI '25 Fig. 11).
  • Semantic zoom (Content) — Pinch or scroll appends and removes attributes from shownAttributes, with the person choosing which attributes survive each zoom level (UIST '25 D1-3).
  • Direct manipulation to spec moves (Layout) — Drag an item beside another to make a grid, flatten it to make a table, shrink it to a node to make a canvas; option-drag attributes to spawn a view (UIST '25 D1-4).
  • Spec exchange (Invocation) — Copy a specification from one site and apply it to another; an extension carries a personal lens across menus and shops (UIST '25 D1-2).

    
Protocol
Sample. Similarweb top 50 US sites; Semrush top 5 in each of 33 categories; 20 random WordPress showcase sites; 20 random Awwwards 2024 Sites of the Year (156 sites, 303 instances).
Unit. One overview→detail relationship; a page with two overviews linked to one detail view counts twice.

    
Relations

    
Usage
  • Hoarders never hide attributes; minimalists hide deliberately and keep the space clean (CHI '25 §7.2)
  • Some configure at the start, others throughout the task (CHI '25 Fig. 21)
  • Surface-then-sort and surface-then-filter sequences
  • Multiple overviews used to structure sub-tasks, such as work vs home monitors

    
Questions
  • How should collection-level attributes be surfaced and computed?
  • Should people choose how detail views are invoked, such as hover and a less maximized view?
  • Which defaults suit which user groups, so fewer customizations are needed?
  • What does surfacing a detail attribute cost when every detail view is its own REST call?

      Techniques · signature Unroll
      • Unroll (Visible items) — Turn any carousel into a grid or list in place, so nothing hides off-screen; the escape hatch every carousel should carry.

      Protocol
      Sample. Home screens of streaming, retail and news apps.

      Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.83 first pass → 0.84 final; all three agree on 90% → 89% of cells. 0 variations adopted of 4 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 1 unobserved variation.

      • Most people see only the first few slides
      
    
      Questions
      • Is Unroll enough to make carousels acceptable where they hide important content?

      • Routes — The means of moving

      Structure composition
      How are places related to each other?
      architecture Information architecture one
      depth Depth one
      Persistent navigation layout
      Where do the always-available routes live?
      placement Placement one
      
      
    
      Wayfinding cues feedback
      How does a person know where they are?
      cues Location cues many
      
      
    
      Routes invocation
      How does a person move?
      routes Ways to move many

      responsive Responsive navigation one

      In the wild
      Productivity tools let people pin, reorder and section their navigation; consumer apps rarely do.
      • Slack — Custom sidebar sections
      • Discord — Server folders
      • Notion — Favourites in the sidebar
      
    
      Techniques · signature Pin anything as a place
      • Pin anything as a place (Persistent navigation) — Any location, saved filter or query can be pinned into persistent navigation, so people build their own architecture on top of the designer’s.
      • Navigation morph (Across devices) — One navigation spec renders as sidebar, rail, tabs or palette, and the person chooses per device.
      • Take me there, show me how · AI (Routes) — “Where do I change billing?” navigates and draws the route it took, so the next time needs no help.
      
    
      Protocol
      Sample. Top 50 apps and sites across categories; record every persistent navigation surface and route type.
      Unit. One product’s navigation system on one platform.
      
      
      Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.71 first pass → 0.96 final; all three agree on 78% → 97% of cells. 6 variations adopted of 7 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 6 unobserved variations.
      
    
      
    
      Relations
      
    
      Usage
      • Experts abandon menus for search and shortcuts; novices rely on visible structure
      
    
      Questions
      • Can a personal architecture coexist with shared documentation that describes the default?

            In the wild
            Autofill is the only widespread end-user lever.
            • Browsers — Autofill profiles
            
    
            Techniques · signature Optional field folding
            • Optional field folding (Grouping) — Fold away optional fields you never fill, pin the ones you always do, remembered per form.
            • Paste to fill · AI (Prefill) — Paste a block of text or drop a document; fields fill with inferred values highlighted for confirmation.
            • Forgiving formats (Validation) — Accept any reasonable format and show the interpretation instead of an error.
            
    
            Protocol
            Sample. Government services, sign-up and checkout, insurance quotes, health intake.

            Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.50 first pass → 0.88 final; all three agree on 68% → 93% of cells. 7 variations adopted of 8 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 9 unobserved variations.
            
      
            Unreliable sub-dimensions. columns
            
    
            
    
            Relations
            
    
            Usage
            • Placeholder-as-label forms fail people who pause mid-entry
            
    
            Questions
            • Can a form be personal without becoming inconsistent with the data the organization needs?

                        Configure
                        
    
                        In the wild
                        Creative professionals routinely customize workspaces, toolbars, shortcuts and plugins.
                        • Photoshop — Saved workspaces and custom shortcuts
                        • Figma — Plugins and widgets
                        • VS Code — Extensions, settings and keybindings
                        
    
                        Techniques · signature Attributes as objects
                        • Attributes as objects (Object structure) — Styles and properties become first-class objects that can be applied, linked and searched, after Object-Oriented Drawing (Xia et al. CHI '16), which CHI '25 builds on.
                        • Select by attribute (Selection) — Form and operate on aggregate selections by shared attribute values, after Collection Objects (Xia et al. CHI '17).
                        • Variations of this · AI (Generation) — Generate alternatives for the selection, laid out side by side as a small design space to compare and blend.
                        
    
                        Protocol

                        Keep track of changing state, and be interrupted only when it matters.
                        
      
                        
    
                        
    
                        Anatomy
                        • Signals — What is watched
                        • Surfaces — Where change shows
                        • Thresholds — When it matters
                        • Responses — What a person can do about it
                        
    
                        Design space
                        Signals content
                        What is being watched?
                        signal Signal type many
                        Surfaces layout
                        Where does change appear?
                        surface Surface many
                        
      
      
    
                        Delivery timing lifecycle
                        When does a change reach the person?
                        timing Timing one
                        What matters initiative
                        Who decides what is worth attention?
                        definition Definition one
                        Severity feedback
                        How is urgency expressed?
                        severity Severity one
                        Granularity scope
                        At what level is state reported?
                        granularity Granularity one
                        
    
                        Configure
                        
    
                        In the wild
                        Notification settings are common but coarse: per app, rarely per condition.
                        • iOS — Focus modes and Scheduled Summary
                        • GitHub — Custom notification routing
                        
    
                        Techniques · signature Attention budget
                        • Attention budget (Delivery timing) — A person sets how many interruptions a period may hold; the system ranks what spends it and batches the rest.
                        • Tell me when this matters · AI (What matters) — A sentence becomes a visible rule with a threshold that can be edited.
                        
    
                        Protocol
                        Sample. Monitoring, banking, delivery, smart-home and collaboration apps.
                        Unit. One monitoring experience.
                        
      
                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.68 first pass → 0.95 final; all three agree on 82% → 97% of cells. 2 variations adopted of 2 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 4 unobserved variations.
                        
    
                        
    
                        Relations
                        
    
                        Usage
                        • People disable whole channels rather than tune them
                        
    
                        Questions
                        • Can one attention model span every app a person uses?

                        • Event — One change
                        • Actor — Who did it
                        • Subject — What it happened to
                        • Filters — Narrowing the record
                        
    
                        Design space
                        Event detail content
                        How much does each event say?
                        detail Detail one
                        Subject scope
                        Whose activity is it?
                        subject Subject one
                        Aggregation composition
                        Are events combined?
                        aggregation Aggregation one
                        Presentation layout
                        How is the record drawn?
                        presentation Presentation one
                        Acting on history invocation
                        Can the past be restored from the log?
                        actions Actions one
                        
      
    
                        
    
                        Configure
                        
    
                        In the wild
                        Filtering by actor or type is common; the representation is fixed.
                        • Google My Activity — Filter by date and product
                        
    
                        Techniques · signature Log as an overview
                        • Log as an overview (Event detail) — Events are items with attributes (who, which field, when) that can be surfaced, sorted and filtered like any overview.
                        • What changed since I looked · AI (Aggregation) — A summary of changes since the person’s last visit, every line linked to its events.
                        
    
                        Protocol
                        Sample. Issue trackers, document tools, admin consoles and personal data dashboards.
                        Unit. One activity record view.
                        
      
                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.77 first pass → 0.93 final; all three agree on 80% → 94% of cells. 1 variation adopted of 1 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 3 unobserved variations.
                        
    
                        
    
                        Relations
                        
    
                        Usage
                        • Logs are read only when something has gone wrong
                        
    
                        Questions
                        • What is the right overview of history: events, versions or people?

                        • Grid — Their arrangement

                        purpose Purpose one
                        Arrangement layout
                        How are widgets placed, and how many?
                        arrangement Arrangement one
                        density Density one
                        Linking composition
                        How do widgets affect each other?
                        linking Linking one
                        Refresh lifecycle
                        How current is it?
                        refresh Refresh one
                        
      
    
                        Alerting feedback
                        How does it call attention to change?
                        alerting Alerting one
                        Ownership collaboration
                        Whose dashboard is it?
                        ownership Ownership one
                        
    
                        Configure
                        
    
                        In the wild
                        Analytics and monitoring tools let people edit panels; most product dashboards are fixed.
                        • Grafana — Edit panels, variables and layout
                        • Datadog — Custom dashboards
                        
    
                        Techniques · signature Tile surfacing
                        • Tile surfacing (Widgets and purpose) — Pull any metric from a drill-down page up onto the dashboard as a tile: Fluid Attributes from detail to overview.
                        • Dashboard from a question · AI (Widgets and purpose) — “How is onboarding going?” proposes widgets with the queries shown, to keep or discard.
                        • Arrange by glance frequency (Arrangement) — Tiles a person looks at most drift to where the eye lands first, with the move proposed rather than imposed.
                        
    
                        Protocol
                        Sample. Analytics, monitoring, finance, fitness and admin products.
                        Unit. One dashboard.
                        
      
                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.59 first pass → 0.95 final; all three agree on 71% → 96% of cells. 4 variations adopted of 4 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 7 unobserved variations.
                        
    
                        
    
                        Relations
                        
    
                        Usage
                        • Shared dashboards accumulate tiles no one remembers adding
                        
    
                        Questions
                        • Is a dashboard an overview whose items are metrics, with drill-downs as detail views?

                        surface Surface one

                        bulk Bulk many
                        
    
                        Configure
                        
    
                        In the wild
                        Per-app settings and focus modes exist; conditions and rules rarely do.
                        • iOS — Focus modes and summaries
                        • GitHub — Filter by reason and custom filters
                        
    
                        Techniques · signature Reason filters
                        • Reason filters (Bulk handling) — Filter by why a notification exists, then turn any filter into a rule for what arrives in future.
                        • Summaries with sources · AI (What arrives) — Stacks collapse into a summary whose every line opens the notification it came from.
                        
    
                        Protocol

                        • Should the notification centre and the inbox be the same overview?

                        Techniques · signature Pick my milestones
                        • Pick my milestones (Updates) — People choose which stage changes notify them, and where: lock screen, email or nothing.

                        Relations

                        • How should uncertainty in an estimate be shown?

                              Techniques · signature Show me in my interface
                              • Show me in my interface (Placement) — Help highlights and demonstrates on the person’s actual, possibly customized, interface, never on a stock screenshot.

                                Onboarding tour

                                Anatomy
                                • Steps — Each introduction
                                • Anchor — The feature being shown
                                • Progress — How many remain
                                • Exit — Skip or finish
                                
    
                                Design space
                                Form layout

                                form Form one

                                progression Progression one
                                Action required initiative
                                Does the person do or just read?
                                action Action one

                                reaccess Re-access one
                                
    
                                Configure
                                
    
                                In the wild
                                Skipping is the only lever.
                                  
    
                                  Techniques · signature Tour from my goal

                                        Plan in time
                                        
        
                                        Arrange things along time and coordinate availability with others — the activity behind calendars, booking slots, project plans and personal to-dos.
                                        
      
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Anatomy
                                        • Time axis — How duration and position are represented
                                        • Events or tasks — Things placed on or ordered by time
                                        • Availability — When people or resources are free
                                        • Coordination — How schedules meet across people
                                        
    
                                        Design space
                                        Time representation encoding
                                        How is time made visible, and at what grain?
                                        granularity Granularity one
                                        scale Scale control one
                                        Placement and conflict composition
                                        How do items sit relative to each other on time, and what happens when they overlap?
                                        placement Placement model one
                                        
      
    
                                        conflicts Conflicts many
                                        Whose time scope
                                        Whose calendar or availability is in play?
                                        whoseTime Scope of people and resources one
                                        Editing commitment lifecycle
                                        When does placing something become binding, and how does it change later?
                                        commitment Commitment one
                                        
    
                                        Configure
                                        
    
                                        In the wild
                                        View grain and which calendars are overlaid are routinely personal; conflict policy and placement model almost never are.
                                        • Google Calendar — Day/Week/Month/Schedule and custom working hours
                                        • Outlook — Overlay and overlay colour per calendar
                                        • Notion — Calendar vs timeline vs list views of the same database
                                        
    
                                        Techniques · signature Scale as a first-class attribute
                                        • Scale as a first-class attribute (Time representation) — Treat view grain as a bindable attribute of the schedule: zoom changes which fields appear on events, as semantic zoom does for collection attributes.
                                        • Conflict as a surfaced attribute (Placement and conflict) — Expose clash, free/busy and travel buffers as attributes that can be filtered, sorted and colour-encoded rather than only as warnings.
                                        • Propose a mutual window · AI (Whose time) — Given constraints in words (“after school, under 45 minutes, no Fridays”), propose candidate slots with inspectable sources from each calendar.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Calendar, scheduling, project-management and booking products across productivity, enterprise, health and travel; code every surface whose main job is placing or finding time.
                                        Unit. One schedule surface for one set of people or resources (a screen can hold several).
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.77 first pass → 0.96 final; all three agree on 84% → 98% of cells. 1 variation adopted of 1 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 2 unobserved variations.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • People switch grain mid-task (month to find a free day, then day to place the hour)
                                        • Busy professionals treat conflict visibility as more important than event aesthetics
                                        
    
                                        Questions
                                        • Is there one schedule grammar under calendar, Gantt and task list, or do absolute vs relative time need separate spaces?
                                        • How should personal working hours travel across products the way a Meridian spec travels across shops?

                                        Availability picker
                                        
        
                                        A surface for choosing a free time from offered or computed availability — for booking someone else, polling a group, or finding mutual free slots.
                                        
      
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Anatomy
                                        • Availability window — When booking is allowed
                                        • Slot grid or list — Candidate times
                                        • Duration control — How long the meeting is
                                        • Confirmation — The held or booked time
                                        
    
                                        Design space
                                        How availability is defined content
                                        What makes a slot free, and what does the booker see?
                                        availSource Source of free/busy one
                                        slotDisclosure Slot disclosure one
                                        Choosing a slot flow
                                        What is the path from browsing times to a hold?
                                        selectionPath Selection path one
                                        Slot presentation layout
                                        How are candidate times arranged?
                                        slotLayout Arrangement one
                                        
      
      
      
    
                                        Constraints and buffers scope
                                        What rules shrink the set of bookable times?
                                        constraints Constraints many
                                        
      
    
                                        Hold and confirm lifecycle
                                        When is the slot reserved, and how long does a hold last?
                                        holdBehaviour Hold behaviour one
                                        Who drives initiative
                                        Who proposes times — host, guest or system?
                                        initiative Initiative one
                                        
    
                                        Configure
                                        
    
                                        In the wild
                                        Hosts configure hours and buffers; guests almost never reshape how slots are shown.
                                        • Calendly — Host availability rules and meeting types
                                        • Google Calendar Appointment schedules — Booking page settings
                                        
    
                                        Techniques · signature Constraint as attributes
                                        • Constraint as attributes (Constraints and buffers) — Expose notice, buffer, duration and timezone as filterable attributes on the slot set so guests can narrow (“only after 5pm in my timezone”).
                                        • Explain why unavailable (How availability is defined) — Grey slots carry a reason code (outside hours, buffer, conflict, capacity) visible on demand without leaking private event titles.
                                        • Negotiate in language · AI (Who drives) — “Sometime next week that doesn’t conflict with school pickup” becomes ranked slots with inspectable constraints from both sides.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Calendly, SavvyCal, Doodle, Google Appointment schedules, Outlook Scheduling Assistant, OpenTable, Mindbody and clinic patient portals.
                                        Unit. One booking or find-a-time session between host(s) and guest(s).
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.62 first pass → 0.95 final; all three agree on 75% → 95% of cells. 4 variations adopted of 5 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 6 unobserved variations.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • Guests abandon when timezone or duration is wrong; hosts over-constrain and starve the slot list
                                        
    
                                        Questions
                                        • How much conflict reason can be shown without leaking privacy?
                                        • Should guests be allowed to request outside declared hours as a first-class path?

                                        In the wild
                                        View choice, overlays and working hours are common personal settings; grid field density and invite policy are rarely end-user malleable.
                                        • Google Calendar — View switcher, calendar toggles, working location
                                        • Outlook — Overlay mode and conditional formatting
                                        • Apple Calendar — Delegate and shared calendar toggles
                                        
    
                                        Techniques · signature Fluid event fields
                                        • Fluid event fields (Event content) — Surface or hide attributes from event detail onto every grid block (travel time, video link, project tag) per person, as Fluid Attributes does for collections.
                                        • View morph with selection held (View structure) — Switch day/week/month/agenda while keeping the selected event and scroll anchor, so grain changes without losing place.
                                        • Schedule from intent · AI (Creating and moving) — “Find two hours with Ana next week near campus” proposes ranked slots with sources from each calendar and travel estimates.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar, Fantastical, Fastmail, and calendar views inside Notion, Linear and university LMS products.
                                        Unit. One calendar surface (one account’s visible calendars in one view mode).
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.65 first pass → 0.93 final; all three agree on 75% → 95% of cells. 0 variations adopted of 0 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 8 unobserved variations.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • People overlay calendars to negotiate; they hide calendars to focus
                                        • Drag-create is preferred on desktop; list-create on mobile

                                        • Which event attributes deserve to be first-class on the grid without creating clutter?
                                        • Can a personal calendar lens (fields + overlays) transfer across Google and Outlook?

                                        • Time axis — Days, weeks or months along the top

                                        • Today marker — The current date on the axis

                                        chrome Chrome one
                                        ganttScale Scale one
                                        Editing bars invocation
                                        How are start, end and links changed?
                                        editGestures Edit gestures many
                                        Planning vs tracking feedback
                                        How does the timeline show plan quality and slippage?
                                        statusFeedback Status feedback many
                                        Whose plan collaboration
                                        Who can edit, and how are parallel plans reconciled?
                                        sharing Sharing one

                                        In the wild
                                        Zoom, grouping and which fields appear on bars are often configurable in PM tools; dependency semantics rarely are.
                                        • Jira Timeline — Zoom and field display
                                        • Asana Timeline — Sort, colour and dependency toggles
                                        • Notion — Timeline view properties and group by
                                        
    
                                        Techniques · signature Fluid bar fields
                                        • Fluid bar fields (Bar and row content) — Surface any task attribute onto bars (risk, estimate, team) and use it for colour or label; hide the rest per viewer.
                                        • Dependency preview (Dependencies and constraints) — While dragging, show which successors will move and by how much before release.
                                        • Replan from a goal date · AI (Planning vs tracking) — “Hit launch by June 1” proposes date shifts and flags impossible dependencies with inspectable rationale.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira Timeline / Advanced Roadmaps, Asana Timeline, Linear initiatives, Notion timeline, Primavera.
                                        Unit. One timeline view over one project or portfolio.
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.55 first pass → 0.93 final; all three agree on 67% → 95% of cells. 0 variations adopted of 0 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 3 unobserved variations.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • Managers live in roll-ups; contributors edit leaf bars
                                        • Zoom out for executive narrative, zoom in to schedule

                                        List apps routinely let people choose grouping, visible fields and smart filters; that malleability is the product.

                                        • Linear — Display options and custom views

                                        Techniques · signature Surface then sort the work
                                        • Surface then sort the work (Task representation) — Any field surfaced on the row becomes a sort, group and filter key — the collection finding applied to tasks.
                                        • Plan date vs due date (Scheduling link) — Keep deadline and intended work time as separate attributes so lists and calendars can bind differently without fighting.
                                        • Break this down · AI (Ordering and grouping) — “Make this shippable by Friday” proposes sub-tasks with estimates and due dates, each editable before accept.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Todoist, Things, Apple Reminders, Microsoft To Do, Google Tasks, Asana list views, Linear, Notion task databases, TickTick.
                                        Unit. One list or smart view over a set of tasks.
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.64 first pass → 0.89 final; all three agree on 75% → 91% of cells. 1 variation adopted of 1 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 1 unobserved variation.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • Daily planners live in Today views; managers live in assigned-to-me filters
                                        • People capture quickly and triage later

                                        • How much hierarchy helps before an outline becomes a project plan in disguise?

                                        In the wild
                                        Layer toggles and map type (default / satellite) are common; projection choice and selection model almost never are end-user controllable.
                                        • Google Maps — Layers, map type, and saved lists
                                        • Miro — Frame and zoom-to-fit habits
                                        • Figma — Zoom percentage and multiplayer cursors
                                        
    
                                        Techniques · signature Semantic zoom as content policy
                                        • Semantic zoom as content policy (Projection and scale) — Bind which attributes and mark types appear to scale bands, so zooming is not only geometric but a content filter the person can edit.
                                        • Space then detail (Selection and detail) — Treat spatial marks as an overview and the attached card or inspector as detail, with the same Fluid Attributes grammar as CHI '25 collections.
                                        • Find a place that fits · AI (Located content) — “Quiet cafés open now within a ten-minute walk” filters and ranks marks with inspectable criteria on the map.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Maps, indoor wayfinding, ticketing seat maps, whiteboards, design canvases, Earth viewers and 3D product/model viewers across app stores and the web.
                                        Unit. One spatial viewport over one world (a product may host several worlds).
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.72 first pass → 0.89 final; all three agree on 84% → 93% of cells. 5 variations adopted of 7 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 1 unobserved variation.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • People zoom out to orient, zoom in to decide
                                        • Search often precedes pan when the destination is known by name
                                        
    
                                        Questions
                                        • Is geographic map, canvas and 3D one design space with different projections, or three?
                                        • Which spatial customizations should travel with the person across products?

                                        Mark encoding encoding

                                        In the wild
                                        Layer and basemap toggles are common; mark encodings and coupling layout are rarely personal.

                                        • Airbnb — Search as I move and price-on-map
                                        • Strava — Heatmap and activity filters
                                        
    
                                        Techniques · signature Fluid map attributes
                                        • Fluid map attributes (Mark encoding) — Surface any place attribute onto pins (price, rating, open-now) and let colour/size/label bind to it per person.
                                        • Fit to the filtered set (Map and list coupling) — Changing filters always offers zoom-to-fit the remaining marks without stealing the user’s manual viewport unless asked.
                                        • Describe the area · AI (Filtering the world) — “Family-friendly spots near the park that are quiet after 8” becomes a filter layer with visible criteria chips.
                                        
    
                                        Protocol
                                        Sample. Google Maps, Apple Maps, Airbnb, Zillow, Uber, Citymapper, Strava, news and election maps, and government GIS viewers.
                                        Unit. One map viewport with its active layers and coupled list/detail, if any.
                                        
      
                                        Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.61 first pass → 0.89 final; all three agree on 75% → 93% of cells. 0 variations adopted of 0 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 2 unobserved variations.
                                        
    
                                        
    
                                        Relations
                                        
    
                                        Usage
                                        • People alternate search-then-map and map-then-filter
                                        • Price-on-pin changes decision speed in lodging and tickets

                                          How is intent handed to the model?
                                          handoff Handoff many
                                          Initiative balance initiative
                                          Who drives the next step?
                                          initiative Initiative one
                                          Verification feedback
                                          How does the person know what the model did and whether to trust it?
                                          verification Verification many
                                          Acceptance scope scope
                                          What can be accepted, edited or undone?
                                          scope Scope one
                                          
    
                                          Configure
                                          
    
                                          In the wild
                                          Model, tone and tool permissions are increasingly user-set; verification UI less so.
                                          • ChatGPT — Custom instructions and model picker
                                          • Cursor — Rules, model choice, apply controls
                                          • Midjourney — Parameters and remix
                                          
    
                                          Techniques · signature Intent as an editable brief
                                          • Intent as an editable brief (Handoff form) — Promote the prompt into a visible brief (goal, constraints, context, tools) whose parts can be edited between runs.
                                          • Never silent apply (Verification) — Default to reviewable diffs, citations or previews before mutating the user’s artifact.
                                          
    
                                          Protocol
                                          Sample. Chat assistants, coding copilots, image generators and agent products.
                                          Unit. One delegation episode from intent through acceptance.
                                          
      
                                          Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.85 first pass → 0.85 final; all three agree on 91% → 91% of cells. 0 variations adopted of 0 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 1 unobserved variation.
                                          
    
                                          
    
                                          Relations
                                          
    
                                          Usage
                                          • People paste outputs elsewhere when apply and provenance are weak
                                          
    
                                          Questions
                                          • What minimum provenance makes acceptance responsible rather than ritual?

                                          Agent run
                                          
        
                                          A goal-directed model session that plans and executes multiple steps with tools, while the person monitors, interrupts, approves and reviews the resulting changes.
                                          
      
                                          
    
                                          
    
                                          Anatomy
                                          • Goal — The assigned objective
                                          • Plan or trace — Steps the agent takes
                                          • Tools — Actions it may invoke
                                          • Artifacts — Files or states it changes
                                          • Approval gates — Human checkpoints
                                          
    
                                          Design space
                                          Goal briefing content
                                          What specifies the agent’s job?
                                          brief Brief many
                                          Step composition composition
                                          How are steps, tools and artifacts structured?
                                          structure Structure one
                                          Run control invocation
                                          How is a run started, steered and stopped?
                                          control Control many
                                          Autonomy lifecycle lifecycle
                                          How long does the agent act without a person?
                                          lifecycle Lifecycle one
                                          Progress feedback feedback
                                          How does the person see what the agent is doing?
                                          feedback Feedback many
                                          
      
      
    
                                          Approval initiative initiative
                                          When must a person act during the run?
                                          approvals Approvals one
                                          
      
      
    
                                          
    
                                          Configure
                                          
    
                                          In the wild
                                          Tool permissions, models and approval strictness are increasingly configurable.
                                          • Cursor — Agent mode, rules, apply controls
                                          • ChatGPT — Agent / operator permissions
                                          • GitHub Copilot coding agent — Repo access and PR flow
                                          
    
                                          Techniques · signature Trace as a first-class log
                                          • Trace as a first-class log (Progress feedback) — Make every tool call, rationale and artifact change a reviewable, filterable event—not only chat prose.
                                          • Risk-tiered approvals (Approval initiative) — Map tool classes to approval policies the person can tighten without stopping harmless reads.
                                          • Redirect without reset · AI (Run control) — Mid-run natural-language redirects amend the brief and continue with provenance of the change.
                                          
    
                                          Protocol
                                          Sample. Coding agents, computer-use agents and multi-step enterprise assistants.
                                          Unit. One goal-directed run with its trace and approvals.
                                          
      
                                          Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.68 first pass → 0.96 final; all three agree on 76% → 97% of cells. 4 variations adopted of 4 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 6 unobserved variations.
                                          
    
                                          
    
                                          Relations
                                          
    
                                          Usage
                                          • People babysit the trace on first runs, then loosen approvals for familiar tasks
                                          
    
                                          Questions
                                          • What is the right unit of approval when an agent edits many files?

                                          AI chat
                                          
        
                                          A turn-taking conversation with a model where prompts and replies accumulate, and the person steers by following up, editing context or starting anew.
                                          
      
                                          
    
                                          
    
                                          Anatomy
                                          • Thread — The turn history
                                          • Composer — Where the next prompt is written
                                          • Reply — A model turn
                                          • Context sources — Files, tools or retrieval attached
                                          • Controls — Regenerate, stop, branch
                                          
    
                                          Design space
                                          Turn content content
                                          What can a turn contain?
                                          turnContent Turn content many
                                          
      
    
                                          Thread composition composition
                                          How do turns and side contexts relate?
                                          composition Composition one
                                          Composer invocation invocation
                                          How is the next message started?
                                          invokeBy Invoke by many
                                          Conversation flow flow
                                          How does the dialogue progress and recover?
                                          flow Flow one
                                          
      
      
      
    
                                          Reply feedback feedback
                                          How is generation and quality communicated?
                                          feedback Feedback many
                                          Context scope scope
                                          What does the model condition on?
                                          scope Scope one
                                          
    
                                          Configure
                                          
    
                                          In the wild
                                          Custom instructions, model choice and memory toggles are common; thread layout less so.
                                          • ChatGPT — Custom instructions, memory, model picker
                                          • Claude — Projects and artifacts
                                          • Perplexity — Focus modes and source controls
                                          
    
                                          Techniques · signature Fork from an edited turn
                                          • Fork from an edited turn (Conversation flow) — Editing a past prompt creates a branch rather than silently rewriting history.
                                          • Show what was grounded (Reply feedback) — Attach retrieval, tool and file provenance to each claim that depends on them.
                                          • Suggest the next ask · AI (Composer invocation) — Offer follow-up chips that deepen, challenge or operationalize the last reply.
                                          
    
                                          Protocol
                                          Sample. Consumer and enterprise chat assistants, sidebar copilots and voice assistants.
                                          Unit. One chat thread with its composer and context bindings.
                                          
      
                                          Coded. 20 instances, 3 raters (fable, opus, sonnet), 3 rounds. κ 0.56 first pass → 0.91 final; all three agree on 68% → 94% of cells. 4 variations adopted of 4 proposed; 0 unresolved cells; 2 unobserved variations.
                                          
    
                                          
    
                                          Relations
                                          
    
                                          Usage
                                          • People start new chats when context pollution is cheaper than steering
                                          
    
                                          Questions
                                          • When should a chat graduate into an artifact or an agent run?
